subject: shiny website for people with disabilities? (tips for Section 508 compliance?)

messages.author: 6e2469edb8d6f53c
messages.subject: shiny website for people with disabilities? (tips for Section 508 compliance?)
parts:
Hi, 
  I like and use shiny a lot to share results within the research group I am in. Now we want to release this shiny website as part of our research publication, and we are planning to do this for many more projects in our group. 

  Has anyone here built shiny-based websites that are accessible to people with disabilities? Specifically shiny websites that are Section 508 compliant (which is a good design principle for a website, and also required by law in federal agencies that we are part of, and those outside including institutes funded by federal agencies; please see http://www.hhs.gov/web/section-508/  http://www.508checker.com/what-is-508-compliance ). 

  I understand that the level of interactivity in shiny could sometimes be irreconcilable with section 508, however the key is if a good-faith effort is put in to make the website accessible. For instance, is there any effort by the developers or workaround by users to address html tags such as "alt" tags for interactive images produced by shiny (please see here: http://www.hhs.gov/web/section-508/making-files-accessible/checklist/html/index.html for more on alt tags)?  

Thanks, 
Mani
